title: Socio-economic data for your research — without months of fieldwork.
text:
Proof of concept — for Tanzanian universities 

Socio-economic data for your research — without months of fieldwork.


Takwimu Bridge (placeholder name) is a curated catalog of Tanzanian socio-economic datasets. Browse a topic, request access, and download — so students spend less time collecting data and more time analyzing it.


  Browse Data   Learn More 




9


Sample Datasets




9


Topic Categories




5


Partner Universities*




*Placeholder partners shown for demonstration — see For Universities.













The Problem

Fieldwork is slow, costly, and often out of reach.


Many undergraduate and postgraduate research projects stall at the data collection stage. Household surveys and enumeration take weeks, travel and logistics strain student budgets, and small self-collected samples limit how far a dissertation’s analysis can go.


Meanwhile, high-quality socio-economic survey data already exists — collected by national statistics agencies, research institutes, and development partners — but it is scattered, hard to discover, and rarely packaged for classroom or thesis use.








Weeks lost


to travel & enumeration







High cost


of independent fieldwork







Small samples


limit statistical power







Hard to discover


existing quality datasets












How It Works

From browsing to your dataset, in four steps


A simple, transparent workflow designed around how student research actually happens.






1


 Browse


Search and filter the catalog by topic, region, and year to find the dataset your research needs.






2


 Request


Submit a short access request describing your research purpose and supervisor details.






3


 Get Approved


An administrator reviews the request and approves access under the dataset’s usage terms.






4


 Download


Download the dataset and citation details, ready to bring into your analysis.





 In this proof of concept, steps 3–4 are demonstrated as mock states — see the Guidelines & FAQ page for what’s real vs. simulated.

title: About Takwimu Bridge
text:
Takwimu Bridge (placeholder name) exists to give Tanzanian university students faster, more reliable access to quality socio-economic data — so that research time goes into analysis and insight, not into the logistics of fieldwork.
We curate datasets already collected by national statistics agencies, research institutes, and development partners, and make them discoverable, well-documented, and citation-ready for coursework, dissertations, and early-career research.

text:
Takwimu Bridge (placeholder name) exists to give Tanzanian university students faster, more reliable access to quality socio-economic data — so that research time goes into analysis and insight, not into the logistics of fieldwork.
We curate datasets already collected by national statistics agencies, research institutes, and development partners, and make them discoverable, well-documented, and citation-ready for coursework, dissertations, and early-career research.

title: About Takwimu Bridge
text:
The Problem We’re Addressing
Independent data collection is often the biggest bottleneck in student research:

Time. Designing instruments, training enumerators, and traveling to field sites can consume months that a degree timeline doesn’t have.
Cost. Transport, accommodation, and enumerator payments are significant out-of-pocket costs for most students.
Sample size. Self-collected samples are often too small for robust statistical analysis, limiting the strength of a thesis’s conclusions.
Discoverability. High-quality datasets already exist, but they are scattered across agency websites, PDFs, and restricted repositories that are hard for a student to find or interpret.

Takwimu Bridge addresses this by centralizing a curated, well-described catalog in one place, with a simple, transparent request-and-approval process.

title: About Takwimu Bridge
text:
How University Recognition Works
For datasets to be trusted for academic use, participating universities review and endorse the portal’s data-use terms, citation standards, and request workflow — much like a university library endorses a database subscription. A partner university’s students then use their institutional affiliation when requesting datasets, and supervisors can be looped in on requests for oversight.
Read more on the For Universities & Partners page about what formal recognition involves.






Note  Proof-of-concept status



This is an early proof of concept built to demonstrate the user experience of browsing, requesting, and (eventually) downloading datasets. No university has formally endorsed this specific demo site — the partner list and logos shown throughout are illustrative placeholders.

text:
Note  Demo terms



The terms below are placeholder/illustrative language for this proof of concept, modeled on common academic data-sharing agreements. They are not a legally reviewed policy.



Academic, non-commercial use only. Datasets on this portal may be used for coursework, theses, dissertations, and non-commercial research.
No redistribution. Do not re-publish or redistribute raw data files outside your research team without permission.
Attribution required. Always cite the original data provider and Takwimu Bridge using the suggested citation on each dataset’s page.
Report responsibly. When publishing findings, avoid presenting sample/placeholder figures (in this demo) or small-sample statistics (in production) as nationally representative without appropriate caveats.
Sensitive topics. Datasets covering sensitive subjects (e.g. gender-based violence) may require an additional ethics/IRB clearance in production.

text:
Citation Requirements
Each dataset page includes a Suggested Citation in the Dataset Details section. At minimum, a citation should include: the data provider, the year, the dataset title, “Takwimu Bridge” as the distributing portal, and the retrieval date. Example:

National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). (2022). Tanzania Population and Housing Census — Sample Extract [Data set]. Takwimu Bridge (demo portal). Retrieved 2026-07-29 from https://example.org/datasets/tanzania-population-census.

title: Guidelines & FAQ
text:
The Request Process

Browse the Data Catalog and open a dataset’s detail page.
Click Request Access — this opens the Request Access form with the dataset pre-selected.
Fill in your university, student ID, research purpose, and supervisor details, then agree to the terms above.
(Production) An administrator reviews and approves or follows up on your request; you’re notified by email.
(Production) The Download button unlocks on the dataset’s page.

title: Guidelines & FAQ
text:
Expected Turnaround
3–5 business days is the target turnaround in the intended production workflow (placeholder SLA — to be confirmed with partner universities).

title: Guidelines & FAQ
text:
Frequently Asked Questions
Is this connected to a real database or login system yet? No. This is a static proof-of-concept site. The Request Access form posts to a form-service placeholder, and “Pending Approval” / “Download” states on dataset pages are simulated, not backed by real access control. 
Can I download data right now? Not real data — each dataset page includes a small, clearly-labeled placeholder CSV sample and preview table so you can see the data’s shape, but the Download button itself is disabled to demonstrate the intended gated-access flow.
Who approves requests in production? This would be a nominated administrator — likely a university library staff member or portal maintainer — reviewing requests against the stated research purpose and supervisor confirmation.
What if my university isn’t listed? The university dropdown on the request form is a placeholder list. Select “Other” and note your institution in the Research Purpose field, or reach out via Contact.
Can I request more than one dataset at once? Yes — the “Dataset(s) Requested” field on the request form supports multiple selections.
Is there a cost to use the portal? No — the portal itself is intended to be free for students at partner universities. Individual dataset licenses/terms are shown on each dataset page.

title: For Universities & Partners
text:
University partnership gives your students a vetted, citation-ready data source for coursework and dissertations, without your department having to host or curate the datasets itself. Partnership is designed to be lightweight:

Endorse the terms. Your institution reviews and signs off on the portal’s data-use terms and citation standard.
Nominate a liaison. A librarian, research office staff member, or department coordinator acts as your point of contact and can co-review student requests from your institution.
Promote to students. Students use their university affiliation when requesting datasets, so requests can be routed and reported per institution.
